claims.text: Pipelines are defined in .dip files using the Dippin DSL, with workflow headers declaring goal, start, exit, defaults (model/provider), and edges between nodes.
Workflows can declare environmental requirements via a requires: header line; as of v0.29.0 only git is checked, and unrecognized entries warn and continue.
Tracker is a three-layer stack: an LLM client with provider adapters, an agent session with turn loop and context compaction, and a pipeline engine with graph execution, checkpoints, and TUI.
The engine supports eight node types: agent, human gate, tool, parallel, fan_in, subgraph, manager_loop, and conditional.
Both build workflows run a SpecLint preflight (dangling refs, contradictory constants, contract mismatches) that fails closed before decomposition.
Human gates support five modes: choice, freeform, hybrid, yes/no, and interview, with interview answers stored as JSON plus a markdown summary.
Headless operation is supported via --webhook-url: human gates are POSTed as JSON and the pipeline resumes on callback, with flags for timeout, timeout action, and auth header.
Each agent node runs a fresh LLM session; data flows between nodes via context keys (ctx.*, params.*, graph.*), not conversation history, with per-node scoping available.
Agent, tool, and interview nodes can declare writes:/reads: context keys; missing declared writes hard-fail the node, and reads: pins fidelity of upstream keys.
Tracker supports four LLM providers: anthropic, openai, gemini, and openai-compat, configured via tracker setup or environment variables stored in ~/.config/2389/tracker/.env.
All providers can be routed through Cloudflare AI Gateway via TRACKER_GATEWAY_URL or --gateway-url, with per-provider base-URL overrides taking precedence over the gateway.
The core engine is UI-agnostic: TUI, Slack bot, and terminal REPL are peers on one library boundary sharing a transport-neutral transport/chatops core.
Variable expansion is single-pass so resolved values are never re-scanned, preventing recursive expansion; unknown --param keys hard-fail at startup.
Secret inputs are staged to a 0600 file and ${inputs.<name>} resolves only to the path, so secret values never enter prompts, the provider wire, traces, or checkpoints.
The working_dir attribute for per-node working directories is validated against path traversal and shell metacharacters.

The superspec workflow includes per-phase mechanical quality gates (build, test, lint, coverage, complexity) and a final TraceabilityAudit gate verifying spec requirements map to implementation and test coverage.
Git artifact commits per terminal node outcome are enabled only via the library's WithGitArtifacts(true) option; the README states there is no CLI flag for this today.
Tracker targets teams running multi-agent LLM build/review pipelines, offering human gates, budget ceilings, audit trails, and front-ends for terminal, TUI, and Slack.
